title: Finite coefficient change for closed support
statement:
Fix the global finite-field datum $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ of [def-weil-finite-field-fiber] and a prime $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}k$. Let $E,L/\mathbf Q_\ell$ be finite extensions, let $m,n\geq1$, and let $\varphi:A\to B$ be a unital homomorphism between the finite coefficient rings $A=A_{E,m}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^m$ and $B=A_{L,n}=\mathcal O_L/\varpi_L^n$ of [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. This includes coefficient reduction and finite coefficient-field extension at compatible levels; flatness of $B$ over $A$ is not assumed. For a separated finite-type $k$-scheme $T$ and a complex $K$ of $A$-module sheaves on $T$ put $K_B=K\otimes_A^LB$, the derived change of rings on constant coefficient sheaves [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings].

Let $X,Z$ be separated finite-type $k$-schemes, let $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ be a closed immersion [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties], and let $M\in D^b_{ctf}(X,A)$ [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude]. Work on the small pro-etale sites, with the finite constructible exceptional inverse image of [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image] and the derived direct image of [def-weil-derived-direct-image]. Then the canonical comparison
$$
b_{i,M}:(Ri_A^!M)\otimes_A^LB\xrightarrow{\sim}Ri_B^!(M_B)
$$
is an isomorphism. It is the adjoint, under $i_{*,B}\dashv Ri_B^!$, of
$$
i_{*,B}((Ri_A^!M)_B)\xrightarrow{\ c_{i,Ri_A^!M}^{-1}\ }(i_{*,A}Ri_A^!M)_B\xrightarrow{\ (\varepsilon_{i,A,M})_B\ }M_B,
$$
where $c_{i,N}:(i_{*,A}N)_B\xrightarrow{\sim}i_{*,B}(N_B)$ is the canonical ordinary direct-image coefficient comparison and $\varepsilon_{i,A,M}$ is the exceptional counit. Both sides lie in $D^b_{ctf}(Z,B)$. The comparison is natural in $M$, commutes with the exceptional counit, and is compatible with composition of closed immersions and successive homomorphisms between finite coefficient stages, under the canonical composition and iterated derived change-of-rings identifications.

For a locally closed immersion $h:W\hookrightarrow X$ of separated finite-type $k$-schemes, choose an open subscheme $V\subseteq X$ and a factorization $W\xrightarrow{k}V\xrightarrow{j}X$ in which $k$ is closed and $j$ is open. The corresponding assertion holds for $Rh^!=Rk^!j^*$: the comparison is the closed comparison applied to $j^*M$, composed with the coefficient comparison for open restriction. It is natural in $M$, has the same exceptional-counit compatibility, respects successive coefficient changes, and respects composition of closed immersions inside the chosen open $V$.

proof.text: Derived change of finite coefficients preserves the domain used here. Indeed [lem-sf-proetale-constructible-origin] and [lem-sf-comparison-tor-amplitude] descend any $K\in D^b_{ctf}(T,A)$, for a separated finite-type $k$-scheme $T$, to a bounded constructible etale $K'$ with the same Tor interval $[a,b]$, where $a\leq b$ is part of the finite-Tor definition (for the zero object one may take $a=b=0$). The schemes in question are Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian]: the base $\operatorname{Spec}k$ is Noetherian since its coordinate ring is a field and its underlying space is a single point. By [lem-sf-etale-flat-constructible], choose an etale model $P\cong K'$ with flat constructible terms, zero outside $[a,b]$. The complexes $P$ and $P\otimes_A B$ are K-flat by clause (1) of [lem-kun-kflat-criteria]; [lem-pur-kflat-change-of-rings] gives flat $B$-module terms for the latter, and [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings] identifies it with $K'_B$. On a stratum and an etale covering trivializing a term of $P$, its tensor with $B$ is constant with value $F\otimes_A B$, a finite $B$-module because both $F$ and $B$ are finite. Thus the new terms are constructible; [thm-constructible-serre] makes their cohomology constructible. The reverse implication of [lem-sf-etale-flat-constructible] gives Tor interval $[a,b]$. The tensor comparison of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback], applied to $\nu_T$ with constant $A$ coefficients and the constant module $B$, identifies $\nu_T^*(K'_B)$ with $K_B$, respecting the $B$ action. Finally [lem-sf-comparison-tor-amplitude] transports this Tor interval and constructibility to the pro-etale site. This argument assumes no finite projective dimension of $B$ over $A$.

source.place: Proof, paragraph 3: finite-Tor domains; explicit scalar-extension argument

proof.text: Set $N=Ri_A^!M$ and choose $a\leq b$ with $M$ of Tor amplitude in $[a,b]$. Apply [thm-sf-preservation-class] with its source $Z$, target $X$, morphism $i$, coefficient field $E$ and level $m$. Both schemes are separated finite-type over the fixed $k$, the prime $\ell$ is invertible, and the closed immersion is separated and finite type. For its finite affine chart family write $D=\max d_U$ and $e=\dim X$, using the theorem's convention $D=0$ for an empty chart family and $e=0$ when $X$ is empty. Clauses (1) and (2) give bounded constructibility and Tor amplitude in $[a-2D,b+2e+1]$, hence $N\in D^b_{ctf}(Z,A)$. Step 1 gives $M_B\in D^b_{ctf}(X,B)$ with the same input interval $[a,b]$. Apply the theorem anew with coefficient field $L$ and level $n$, on the same geometric chart family, to obtain $Ri_B^!M_B\in D^b_{ctf}(Z,B)$. This second application rebinds the coefficient field; clause (3), which varies the level for a fixed coefficient field, is not used to change $E$ into $L$. Step 1 applied to $N$ gives $N_B\in D^b_{ctf}(Z,B)$ as well. Every application uses the constructible exceptional functor of the theorem, on bounded constructible inputs of etale origin, rather than an unrestricted ambient adjoint. These checks justify every later application of finite coefficient direct-image exchange, in particular to $i$ with input $N$, without assuming the desired exceptional coefficient exchange.

source.place: Proof, paragraph 3: justification of finite-Tor domains

proof.text: Let $j:U=X\setminus Z\hookrightarrow X$. By [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-open-subscheme-noetherian], $U$ is Noetherian and quasi-compact. Thus $j$ is quasi-compact; on affine charts it is covered by finitely many principal opens, each with coordinate algebra $R[t]/(ft-1)$, so it is of finite type, and it is separated because an open immersion is a monomorphism and its diagonal is an isomorphism. [prop-sf-localization-all-stages] gives the triangle $i_{*,A}N\xrightarrow{\varepsilon_A}M\xrightarrow{\eta_A}Rj_{*,A}j^*M\to$. Apply the exact change-of-rings functor of [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings], obtaining a distinguished triangle with vertices $(i_{*,A}N)_B,M_B,(Rj_{*,A}j^*M)_B$. Apply [prop-sf-localization-all-stages] again with coefficients $B$ and input $M_B$ to obtain the triangle $i_{*,B}Ri_B^!M_B\xrightarrow{\varepsilon_B}M_B\xrightarrow{\eta_B}Rj_{*,B}j^*M_B\to$. The $Ri^!$ appearing in these triangles is exactly the constructible exceptional inverse image of [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image], because clause (2) of [prop-sf-localization-all-stages] explicitly identifies that adjoint. For a closed immersion the identity-open compactification identifies compact-support direct image with ordinary direct image. Only the stated constructible adjunction is used; no unrestricted ambient exceptional adjoint is asserted.

source.place: Proof, paragraph 1: tensor the closed-support triangle

proof.text: By [lem-sf-pullback-tor-amplitude], $j^*M\in D^b_{ctf}(U,A)$. For [lem-coef-finite-direct-image], $B$ is finite as an $A$-module: its finitely many elements generate it over $A$. The inputs $N$ and $j^*M$ have bounded constructible etale representatives with finite Tor amplitude by step 1 and [lem-sf-pullback-tor-amplitude], so the stated pro-etale realization clause applies. [lem-coef-finite-direct-image] applied to $i,N$ and to $j,j^*M$ gives isomorphisms $c_i:(i_{*,A}N)_B\to i_{*,B}N_B$ and $c_j:(Rj_{*,A}j^*M)_B\to Rj_{*,B}(j^*M)_B$. The finite-level tensor comparison [lem-pur-derived-pullback-tensor-iso] identifies $(j^*M)_B$ with $j^*M_B$; write $d_j$ for the resulting third-vertex isomorphism. This is a $B$-linear identification, using $j^*B_X=B_U$. The square $d_j(\eta_A)_B=\eta_B$ commutes: transpose through $j^*\dashv Rj_*$, whose ordinary adjunction is clause 1 of [fix-prop-adjunctions]; the projection comparison is the adjunct of the pullback counit tensored with $B$, by the explicit $a_{u,M,N}$ and $\pi_{u;M,N}$ formulas of [def-exchange-projection]. The transpose of the left side is therefore the composite of the pulled-back unit with that counit, tensored with $B$, hence the identity by the triangle identity. The transpose of the right side is also the identity. The ordinary adjunction itself is supplied explicitly by [fix-prop-adjunctions], clause 1; no exceptional-admissibility clause of that node is used.

source.place: Proof, paragraph 2: identify first and third terms and the open unit square

proof.text: Rotate the two distinguished triangles of step 3 so that their first two vertices are the middle and third vertices. The commutative square from step 4 and axiom TR3 of [def-weil-triangulated-category] extend $(1_{M_B},d_j)$ to a morphism of the rotated triangles; unrotate it. Thus there is a first component $a:(i_{*,A}N)_B\to i_{*,B}Ri_B^!M_B$ satisfying $\varepsilon_B a=(\varepsilon_A)_B$. The other two components are isomorphisms, so [lem-sf-triangle-morphism-iso] makes $a$ an isomorphism. By [prop-sf-closed-unit-all-stages], $i_{*,B}$ is fully faithful on the bounded constructible categories. Under the adjunction $i_{*,B}\dashv Ri_B^!$, a map $i_{*,B}Q\to i_{*,B}Ri_B^!M_B$ is uniquely determined by its composite with $\varepsilon_B$: full faithfulness and the adjunction identify it with a unique map $Q\to Ri_B^!M_B$. Take $Q=N_B$. The identity for $a$ therefore says precisely that $a c_i^{-1}=i_{*,B}b_{i,M}$, where $b_{i,M}$ is the counit-defined comparison in the statement. It follows that $i_{*,B}b_{i,M}$, and hence $b_{i,M}$, is an isomorphism. This identifies the specified map, rather than just some isomorphism between the two vertices.

source.place: Proof, paragraph 2: identify the first comparison and reflect its isomorphism

proof.text: Naturality follows by taking adjoints of the natural morphisms $(\varepsilon_{i,A,M})_B c_{i,N}^{-1}$. The exceptional-counit compatibility is the defining equation $\varepsilon_{i,B,M_B}\,i_{*,B}b_{i,M}=(\varepsilon_{i,A,M})_B c_{i,N}^{-1}$. There is no choice of a cone map in this equation, because the adjunction is a bijection on the relevant Hom sets.

source.place: Proof, paragraph 3: exceptional counit and naturality

proof.text: For closed immersions $W\xrightarrow{k}Z\xrightarrow{i}X$, [lem-weil-derived-direct-image-composition] identifies $(ik)_*$ with $i_*k_*$. Chaining the two exceptional Hom adjunctions identifies $R(ik)^!$ with $Rk^!Ri^!$; its counit is $\varepsilon_i\circ i_*\varepsilon_k$, as is seen by applying the two Hom bijections to the identity. Compare $b_{ik,M}$ with the two-step map $b_{k,Ri_A^!M}$ followed by $Rk_B^!b_{i,M}$. Transpose both through $i_{*,B}k_{*,B}\dashv Rk_B^!Ri_B^!$. Use the defining equation of step 6 twice. The transpose of the two-step map is $(\varepsilon_{i,A}\circ i_{*,A}\varepsilon_{k,A})_B$ preceded by the inverse of the composite of the ordinary coefficient comparisons for $i$ and $k$. The transpose of $b_{ik,M}$ is the same map, because [lem-coef-finite-direct-image] says these ordinary comparisons respect composition. Injectivity of the chained Hom bijection proves the desired equality. Step 2 also applies to $k$ and to $Ri_A^!M$, so every intermediate object is in the required domain.

source.place: Proof, paragraph 3: composition of closed immersions

proof.text: For finite coefficient maps $A\to B\to C$, choose a K-flat flat-term model $P$ of $K$ by [lem-pc-kflat-resolution]. By [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings] and [lem-pur-kflat-change-of-rings], $P\otimes_A B$ is a K-flat flat-term $B$-model of $K_B$. Thus the iterated derived change is identified with the direct one by the degreewise balancing maps $((p\otimes b)\otimes c)\mapsto p\otimes bc$ and $p\otimes c\mapsto(p\otimes1)\otimes c$. They are inverse chain maps, natural in $P$, and descend through [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent]. These are the tensor reassociations used below. [lem-coef-finite-direct-image] explicitly states that its $B$-linear canonical comparisons satisfy $c_i^{A,C}=c_i^{B,C}\circ(c_i^{A,B})_C$ under this reassociation, including arbitrary finite algebra maps. Apply that equality at $N=Ri_A^!M$. Transpose $b_i^{A,C}$ and $b_{i,M_B}^{B,C}\circ(b_{i,M}^{A,B})_C$ through $i_{*,C}\dashv Ri_C^!$. The defining counit equation of step 6, twice for the second map, and naturality of $c_i$ give in both cases $(\varepsilon_{i,A,M})_C(c_{i,N}^{A,C})^{-1}$. Injectivity of the adjunction Hom bijection proves equality. For identity coefficient change the same equation gives the identity. Step 1 and step 2, reapplied at each finite stage, put all exceptional objects in the required finite-Tor constructible domains.

source.place: Proof, paragraph 3: successive coefficient changes; balancing and the stated direct-image coefficient cocycle

proof.text: Let $h=j\circ k$ be the chosen locally closed factorization $W\xrightarrow{k}V\xrightarrow{j}X$. The Noetherian-open result [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-open-subscheme-noetherian] and the principal-open calculation in step 3 make $j$ separated of finite type. At each coefficient stage $R=A,B$, [thm-sf-comp-composition] gives $Rh_{!,R}=j_{!,R}k_{*,R}$: use the identity-open compactification for the closed $k$ and the identity-proper compactification for the open $j$, in [def-compact-support-direct-image-detailed]. Its domain is the bounded-below etale-origin class. Every bounded constructible input on $W$ has such an origin by [lem-sf-proetale-constructible-origin], and the composition theorem explicitly says that the compact-support functors preserve that class. Thus both applications and their intermediate objects are in its stated domain. By [prop-exc-open-adjoint], the open right adjoint is $j_R^*$. Chaining the closed and open Hom adjunctions gives $Rh_R^!=Rk_R^!j_R^*$, with counit $\epsilon_{h,R}=\epsilon_{j,R}\circ j_{!,R}\epsilon_{k,R}$. The open tensor comparison [lem-pur-derived-pullback-tensor-iso] gives $r_{j,M}:(j_A^*M)_B\xrightarrow{\sim}j_B^*M_B$. By [lem-sf-pullback-tor-amplitude], $j_A^*M$ is finite-Tor constructible. Define $b_{h,M}=Rk_B^!(r_{j,M})\circ b_{k,j_A^*M}$. The closed result and preservation from steps 1–2 show that this is an isomorphism between objects of $D^b_{ctf}(W,B)$.

source.place: Proof, paragraph 3: locally closed factorization, functor domains and definition of its comparison

proof.text:
Here is an actual $B$-linear open coefficient isomorphism, needed to formulate the locally closed counit equation. Put $S_T=(-)_B$ and $V_T=\operatorname{Res}_{A\to B}$ on $T=X,V$. [lem-pur-sheaf-ring-derived-coefficient-adjunction] gives $S_T\dashv V_T$ on the unbounded derived categories. Restriction commutes with forgetting scalars: $j_A^*V_X=V_Vj_B^*$, because both restrict the same complexes and the $A$-action is through $A\to B$. For $Q\in D(V_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$ and $H\in D(X_{\mathrm{proet}},B)$, the scalar adjunction and the two open adjunctions of [prop-exc-open-adjoint] therefore give
$$\operatorname{Hom}_B(S_Xj_{!,A}Q,H)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_A(j_{!,A}Q,V_XH)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_A(Q,V_Vj_B^*H)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_B(j_{!,B}S_VQ,H).$$
The mutually inverse Hom bijections determine mutually inverse maps $e_{j,Q}:S_Xj_{!,A}Q\xrightarrow{\sim}j_{!,B}S_VQ$, natural in $Q$, already in $D(B)$. Under the canonical open tensor identification $r_j:S_Vj_A^*\cong j_B^*S_X$ of [lem-pur-derived-pullback-tensor-iso], their counit equation is
$$\epsilon_{j,B,M_B}\,j_{!,B}(r_{j,M})\,e_{j,j_A^*M}=S_X(\epsilon_{j,A,M}).$$
Indeed transpose both sides through the displayed chain: both become the scalar-adjunction unit at $j_A^*M$, by the two open triangle identities and the coefficient-unit normalization $x\mapsto x\otimes1$. This also specifies the canonical open coefficient map without imposing flatness on $B$.

source.place: Proof, paragraph 3: open coefficient comparison and counit, explicit scalar/open Hom calculation

proof.text:
For $Q$ on $W$ set $c_{h,Q}=j_{!,B}(c_{k,Q})\circ e_{j,k_{*,A}Q}$, with the canonical composition identifications from step 9. This is the compact-support coefficient isomorphism in $D(B)$. Write $N=Rk_A^!j_A^*M$, and put $u=\epsilon_{k,A,j_A^*M}:k_{*,A}N\to j_A^*M$. The closed equation of step 6 and naturality of $\epsilon_{k,B}$ give
$$\epsilon_{h,B,M_B}\,h_{!,B}(b_{h,M})\,c_{h,N}
=\epsilon_{j,B,M_B}\,j_{!,B}(r_{j,M})\,j_{!,B}(u_B)\,e_{j,k_{*,A}N}.$$
Naturality of $e_j$ changes the last two factors to $e_{j,j_A^*M}\,(j_{!,A}u)_B$. The open counit equation from step 10 changes the resulting expression to $(\epsilon_{j,A,M})_B(j_{!,A}u)_B=(\epsilon_{h,A,M})_B$. Cancelling $c_{h,N}$ proves precisely the exceptional-counit compatibility in the statement. Naturality of $b_h$ follows from its two natural factors $b_k$ and $r_j$.

source.place: Proof, paragraph 3: locally closed exceptional counit; substitution and naturality

proof.text:
For $A\to B\to C$, the iterated locally closed map is
$$Rk_C^!(r_j^{B,C})\,b_{k,j_B^*M_B}^{B,C}\,(Rk_B^!(r_j^{A,B})\,b_{k,j_A^*M}^{A,B})_C.$$
Naturality of $b_k^{B,C}$ in $r_j^{A,B}$ rewrites this as
$$Rk_C^!(r_j^{B,C}(r_j^{A,B})_C)\,b_{k,(j_A^*M)_B}^{B,C}(b_{k,j_A^*M}^{A,B})_C.$$
The closed coefficient cocycle (step 8) and the associativity compatibility of [lem-pur-derived-pullback-tensor-iso] reduce it to $Rk_C^!(r_j^{A,C})b_{k,j_A^*M}^{A,C}=b_h^{A,C}$. For another closed immersion $t:W'\hookrightarrow W$, step 7 gives $b_{kt,j_A^*M}=Rt_B^!(b_{k,j_A^*M})\,b_{t,Rk_A^!j_A^*M}$. Substitute this in $b_{jkt,M}=R(kt)_B^!(r_{j,M})b_{kt,j_A^*M}$. Functoriality then yields $b_{jkt,M}=Rt_B^!(b_{jk,M})b_{t,R(jk)_A^!M}$. The chained-adjunction counit on both sides is $\epsilon_j\circ j_!\epsilon_k\circ j_!k_*\epsilon_t$. These are the required successive coefficient and closed-composition compatibilities inside the chosen open $V$.
